summary: Results of a Dexcom-funded study published in the New England Journal of Medicine Wednesday demonstrated that people with Type 2 diabetes who don’t take insulin may benefit from wearing a continuous glucose monitor. Dexcom first shared the results at the American Diabetes Association’s Scientific Sessions this summer. The study found that people who wore a CGM had a larger reduction in hemoglobin A1c than people who received routine care after 26 weeks. The published results come as diabetes tech firms anticipate the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to expand Medicare coverage of CGMs for people with diabetes who don’t take insulin. Having a peer-reviewed publication in a leading medical journal “should be a catalyst” for a CMS decision, William Blair analysts wrote in a research note.
